questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A medical officer is conducting a case-control study and employs matching to select controls similar to the cases. Which of the following types of bias is likely to be reduced as a result?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Confounding bias

Matching controls to be similar to the cases is likely to reduce confounding bias or bias due to confounding factors.

A confounding factor is one that is related to both exposure and disease and is distributed unequally in study and control groups. Irrespective of being associated with the exposure under study, the confounding factor might itself serve as a risk factor for the disease. Hence, the elimination of these confounding factors is essential before carrying out a case-control study.

Matching, which is usually done in analytical studies (such as a case-control study), is the process where the participants in two groups (cases and controls in this case) are matched based on factors that are known to influence the outcome of disease (such as age, gender, race, etc.) to stop the potential confounders from distorting the results.

Other strategies to eliminate confounding factors include randomization, stratified randomization, and restriction.

Other options:
Option A - Recall bias in case-control studies occurs because history recollection is better in the case group as they have a stronger exposure than the control group. This bias can be reduced by decreasing the recall period as much as possible.

Option C - Selection bias is a type of sampling bias that occurs because of the nonrandom allocation of subjects such that the study population is not representative of the target population. The best way to reduce this is by randomization to create groups with similar distributions of known and unknown variables.

Option D - Interviewer bias is a type of bias that occurs because the interviewer is aware of the case group and the hypothesis being tested, which can influence interviews and analysis. This can be reduced by blinding to reduce their influence on interviews and interpretation of outcomes.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The fasting blood glucose levels of a hypothetical population form two overlapping distributions, one of the people with diabetes(B), and another one of the people without diabetes(A) resembling those in the figure shown below. A test was done with the cutoff for diagnosing diabetes as 120mg/ dl, what does the area D represent?
options: Non-diabetics correctly classified as the same
Diabetics correctly classified as the same
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Non-diabetics incorrectly classified as diabetics

Area D represents the false positives (Non-diabetics incorrectly classified as diabetics)

Area C represents the False Negatives (Diabetics incorrectly classified as non-diabetics)

Area B represents the True positives (Diabetics correctly classified as the same) and the false negatives

Area A represents the  True negatives (Non-diabetics correctly classified as the same) and the false positives

Note :

From the above distribution curves, it is apparent that the choice of the cutoff point will determine the sensitivity and specificity of the test.

For example, reducing the cutoff to a lower value will increase the sensitivity, but the specificity will be low and the number of false-positive results will be unacceptably high. Similarly, by plotting on a distribution curve think of what would happen if the cutoff point is increased.

A test can only be 100% specific and 100% sensitive if there is no overlap between the curves, this kind of situation doesn't commonly occur and when it does, the disease may be so obvious that no diagnostic testing is required. Hence it is often best to use a combination of tests to diagnose a disease. A highly sensitive (usually relatively cheap) followed by a more specific test.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: There is an outbreak of buboes in the community. What is the vector responsible for this condition?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Xenopsylla cheopis

The vector for bubonic plague is Xenopsylla cheopis. It is also called a rat flea. It also transmits murine typhus, chiggerosis, and hymenolepsis diminuta. It can be identified by the presence of a conical-shaped head, the presence of thorax, abdomen, and three pairs of legs.

Plague is a zoonotic disease caused by Yersinia pestis. It is a gram-negative, non-motile, coccobacillus that exhibits bipolar staining with special stains like Wayson's stain. The reservoir of infections is wild rodents like field mice, gerbils, skunks, etc. In India, Tatera indica is the main reservoir. The important vector of plague is rat flea, also called Xenopsylla cheopis.

Humans acquire the disease by the bite of an infected flea, by direct contact with the tissues of the infected animal, or by droplet infection from cases of pneumonic plague.

Human plague mainly presents as:

Bubonic plague- This is the most common type of disease. The patient develops a sudden fever, chills, headache, and painful lymphadenitis. Within a few days, the lymph nodes in the groin, axilla, or neck enlarge and are called buboes. This is followed by the suppuration of the buboes. Bubonic plague cannot spread from person to person as the bacilli are locked up in the buboes and do not find a way or easy exit.

Pneumonic plague- It develops as a complication of bubonic-septicemic plague.

Septicemic plague- It occurs when the infection spreads to blood.

Other options

Option B- Species Phlebotomus argentipes, belongs to the group of sand fly. It transmits kala azar. Diseases caused by other species of sand flies are sandfly fever and oriental sore.

Below image shows sand fly

Option C- Ixodes ticks (hard ticks) transmit rocky mountain spotted fever, Russian spring-summer encephalitis, Colorado tick fever, tularemia, tick paralysis and human babesiosis.

Below image shows Ixodes tick

Option D- Female Anopheles mosquitoes are vectors for malaria and filariasis (not in India). They can be identified by the presence of spotted wings. When resting on a surface, they make an angle with the surface.

The below image shows anopheles mosquito.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is the correlation coefficient (R) of the given scattergram?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. -0.9

The given scattergram demonstrates a strong negative correlation between the X and Y variables. The correct correlation coefficient (R) value in this case would be -0.9.
A scattergram is a graph in which the values of two variables are plotted along the two axes. Each point on the graph signifies a pair of values from the same observation. The pattern of the resulting points reveals if any correlation exists. A scattergram with positive correlation (R-value > 0) means high values of one variable are associated with high values of another variable. One with a negative correlation (R-value < 0) means high values of one variable are associated with low values of the other variable.

In the given graph, the data points show increasing values on the x-axis correspond with decreasing values on the y-axis and vice-versa (negative correlation). The “line of best fit” for the given scattergram will have data points closer to the line, demonstrating a strong negative correlation (R-value closer to -1).

Determining a correlation coefficient (R) involves finding the “line of best fit” (an imaginary straight line) to the plotted data points. The closer the data points to this straight line, the stronger the linear correlation between the two variables.

Other options:

Option A: R-value of +0.3 is a weak positive correlation (R-value > 0, closer to 0 than 1), as shown below.

Option B: R-value of +1 is a strong positive correlation (R-value > 0, closer to 1 than 0), as shown below.

Option C: R-value of -0.4 is a weak negative correlation (R-value < 0, closer to 0 than 1), as shown below.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text:
Arrange the following in order of the demographic cycle.

1. Early expanding population

2. Declining population

3. Low stationary population

4. Late expanding population

5. High stationary population
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 5, 1, 4, 3, 2

The correct order according to the demographic cycle is high stationary population (5) --> early expanding population  (1) --> late expanding population (4) --> low stationary population (3) -->  declining population  (2).

The demographic cycle has 5 stages:

• Stage 1: High stationary population
• Stage 2: Early expanding population
• Stage 3: Late expanding population
• Stage 4: Low stationary population
• Stage 5: Declining population

In a high stationary population, there is a high birth rate and a high death rate that cancel each other and the population remains stationary.

The early expanding population is marked by a decline in the death rate but the birth rate stays constant. Many countries in South Asia and Africa are in this phase.

In the late expanding population there is a further fall in the death rate, with the birth rate beginning to fall. The population is still increasing due to a net increase in births. India has entered this phase.

A low stationary population is characterized by low birth and low death rate, and this can result in a stationary population. It has occurred in most industrialized countries as a demographic transition shifting from high birth and high death rates to low birth and low death rates.

A declining population is one where the birth rate is lower than the death rate, causing population decline. Examples include East European countries like Germany and Hungary.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The government of India starts a new initiative where rehabilitation centres are opened across the country to support wounded soldiers from the army with medical and psychological aid. Which level of prevention does this fall under?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Tertiary prevention

The rehabilitation of wounded soldiers where they are in the late phase of pathogenesis falls under the tertiary level of prevention.

The tertiary level of prevention signifies intervention in the late pathogenesis phase. Tertiary prevention can be defined as "all measures available to reduce or limit impairments and disabilities, minimize suffering caused by existing departures from good health, and promote the patient's adjustment to irremediable conditions".

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a town, there are 2500 live births within 6 months. During the same period, 5 women died due to peripartum infection, 5 women died due to electrocution, 2 died due to obstructed labour and 3 died due to postpartum haemorrhage. What is the maternal mortality ratio (MMR)?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 400 per 100000 live births

The MMR in the above scenario is 400 per 100000 live births

MMR = Number of maternal deaths in a period x 100,000 (or 1000)/Number of live births in the same period

In this scenario, only 10 women died due to causes related to pregnancy (5-peripartum infection,2- obstructed labour and 3-postpartum haemorrhage). Only they can be included in the statistics.

So, MMR here = 10 x 100000/2500 = 400 per 100,000 live births.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A study was done to assess nutritional status among young children in rural and urban areas. 30 children in rural and 20 children in urban areas were malnourished. Which of the following tests of significance is the most appropriate in this case?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Chi-square test

The most appropriate test of significance, in this case, is the chi-square test. It is used to compare qualitative data between 2 groups with independent measures.

The Chi-square statistic is a non-parametric (distribution-free) test designed to analyze group differences when the dependent variable is measured at a nominal level.

This statistical test can be used to determine whether the antibiotic was effective or not. The outcome of this study would be either "the antibiotics cured the disease" or "the antibiotics did not cure the disease". Hence this study is having two qualitative variables. Qualitative data, also known as “categorical data,” is defined by a category and grouped by characteristics and are then given a name rather than by a measured numeric expression.

If this study were to study the effect of antibiotics in terms of the growth of bacteria in culture, such as the number of colony-forming units grown with each antibiotic, the study would have quantitative/parametric variables. Then other tests like t-test or ANOVA would be used.

Option B: Paired t-test compares paired data or pre-intervention and post-intervention data of the same group. This doesn't apply here as the groups are not paired.

Option C: The standard error of the mean is calculated for quantitative data, with a measure of central tendency as mean.

Option D: ANOVA is used to compare more than 2 groups.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Diseases in which clinical recovery does not coincide with bacteriological recovery give rise to which kind of carrier?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Convalescent carrier

Diseases in which clinical recovery does not coincide with bacteriological recovery give rise to the convalescent carrier.

In cases of typhoid fever, dysentery (bacillary and amebic), cholera, diphtheria, and whooping cough, patients continue to shed the disease agent during the period of recovery following an illness (convalescence). They pose a serious threat to unprotected household members and those in the immediate environment.

Other options:

Option A: Paradoxical carriers are carriers who acquired the pathogen from another carrier. Example: A carrier with subclinical polio infection acquired the pathogen from another household member, who is also a carrier for poliovirus.

Option B: Incubatory carriers are those who shed infectious agents during the incubation period and can carriers transmit the disease before the onset of symptoms. Examples: measles, mumps, polio, pertussis, influenza, diphtheria, and hepatitis B.

Option D: Healthy carriers acquire the infectious agent but do not develop any symptoms of disease and keep shedding the agent. Examples: Poliomyelitis, cholera, meningococcal meningitis, salmonellosis, and diphtheria.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text:
Match the following thermometers with their applications.

Type of thermometer
Application

1. Dry bulb thermometer
A. The mean radiant temperature

2. Globe thermometer
B. The cooling capacity of the working environment

3. Wet globe thermometer
C. Low air velocities

4. Kata thermometer
D. The air temperature
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 1-D, 2-A, 3-B, 4-C

The correct match is 1-D, 2-A, 3-B, and 4-C.

A dry bulb thermometer is an ordinary thermometer used to measure the air temperature. It is mounted on the Stevenson screen for accurate readings.

A globe thermometer can be used for the direct measurement of the mean radiant temperature of the surroundings. It is affected by both the air temperature and radiant heat.

A wet globe thermometer is used for measuring environmental heat. It exchanges heat with the surroundings by conduction, convection, evaporation, and radiation. The equilibrium temperature of the globe provides a comprehensive measure of the cooling capacity of the work environment.

A kata thermometer was originally used to measure the cooling power of the air. It was used to assess the indices of thermal comfort. Currently, it is used only as an anemometer to measure low air velocities.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: As an intern posted in a PHC, you observe a public water tank disinfected with chlorine. Following this, an orthotolidine-arsenite test is performed. What is/are the parameters measured by this test?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Free and combined chlorine separately

The parameters measured by the orthotolidine-arsenite test (OTA) are free and combined chlorine separately.

It is a modification of the orthotolidine test (OT), that measures free and combined chlorine levels together. (Option C)

In addition, the errors caused by the presence of interfering substances such as nitrites, iron and manganese, that produce yellow colour(positive)with an OT test are overcome by the OTA test.

The OT test is performed by adding 0.1 ml of the reagent containing orthotoludine dissolved in 10% hydrochloric acid to 1 ml of water to be tested. A yellow colour is produced which is matched against suitable standards or colour discs. Commercial equipment is available for this purpose. It is essential to take the reading within 10 seconds after the addition of the reagent to estimate free chlorine in water. The colour that is produced after a lapse of 15-20 minutes, is due to the action of both free and combined chlorine.

The chlorine demand is measured by Horrock’s apparatus. (Option A)

questions.text: Which of the following services are provided under the program represented by the logo below?
options: Quality antenatal care free of cost on 9th of every month
Free transport service between home and institution
Improve quality of care in labor room and maternal OTs
Safe motherhood services including IFA tablets, Td vaccination
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Improve quality of care in labor room and maternal OTs

The logo represents Laqshya. It is an initiative launched by the government of India to improve the quality of care in the labor room and maternal OTs.

Laqshya is expected to improve the quality of care that is provided to the pregnant mother in the labor room and maternity operation theatres, thereby preventing the undesirable adverse outcomes associated with childbirth. This initiative is implemented in government medical colleges (MCs) besides district hospitals (DHs), high delivery load sub-district hospitals (SDHs), and community health centers (CHCs).

The initiative plans to conduct quality certification of labor rooms and also incentivize facilities to achieve the targets outlined. The goal of this initiative is to reduce preventable maternal and newborn mortality, morbidity, and stillbirths associated with the care around delivery in the labor room and maternity OT and ensure respectful maternity care. The complete logo of the program is shown below.

Other options:

Option A: Quality antenatal care (including investigations and drugs) is provided free of cost on the 9th of every month under Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA).

Option B: Free transport service from home to institution, between facilities in case of referral, and back to home is provided free of cost under the Janani-Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK). The main aim of JSSK is to provide no-expense delivery, including a cesarean section, to all pregnant women delivering in public health services.

Option C: Safe motherhood services including IFA tablets, Td vaccination are provided under the Vandematharam scheme which is a voluntary scheme.  It can be volunteered by an OBG specialist, lady doctor/ MBBS doctor, maternity home, or nursing home. The enrolled doctors are instructed to display the 'Vandemataram logo' at their clinic. The respective DMO will provide IFA tablets, OC pills, and Td injections to the Vandematharam doctors/ clinics for free distribution to beneficiaries.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is the requirement to give mass treatment for trachoma in a community?
options: Prevalance of more than 5% of cases in adolescent age groups
Prevelance of more than 5% of cases in children of 1-9 years
Prevalance of more than 10% of cases in children of age 1-9 years
Prevalance of more than 10% of cases in adolescent age groups
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Prevalance of more than 10% of cases in children of age 1-9 years

Prevalence of trachoma cases of more than 10% in children of age group 1-9 years is an important criterion to start mass prophylaxis of antibiotic treatment in the community according to the WHO program to control trachoma.

Trachoma is a form of chronic infective conjunctivitis and is one of the leading causes of blindness. It has an ‘active’ inflammatory stage and a ‘cicatricial’ chronic stage. The active inflammatory stage is more prevalent in children. They present with conjunctival follicles containing Leber cells and corneal Herbert's follicles.

The cicatricial chronic stage is seen in middle age. The patient complains of pain, lacrimation, photophobia, and finally loss of vision.

Trachoma is treated according to the WHO classification using the SAFE strategy (Surgery, Antibiotics, Facial hygiene, and Environmental improvement). Azithromycin is the antibiotic of choice, and surgery involves the correction of trichiasis and entropion.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: An epidemiologist describes a disease outbreak in a graph, as shown in the image below, based on the data received from field investigations. Which of the following could be the cause of such an outbreak?
options: Outbreak of cholera due to contaminated well water
Toxic chemical poisoning from an industrial accident
Food poisoning from a lunch party
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Outbreak of cholera due to contaminated well water

The image shows the common source, multiple exposure epidemic. Among the given options an example of it is outbreak of cholera due to contaminated well water.

A common source, multiple exposure epidemic occurs when a group of people are repeatedly exposed to the same harmful source over an extended period, leading to a series of illness cases. This type of epidemic is characterised by multiple peaks in the incident cases, reflecting the ongoing exposure to the source.

Some examples include:

• Legionnaires' disease from a hotel's water system
• Gonorrhea from a sex worker

Common source, single exposure
Common source, multiple exposures

Nature of exposure
Single, brief exposure
Multiple, continuous, or intermittent exposures for a prolonged time

Nature of epidemic
Explosive with clustering of cases within a short interval of time
Less chance of clustering of cases within a short interval of time

Duration of epidemic
Falls within one incubation period of a particular disease
Extends beyond one incubation period of a particular disease

Example
An epidemic of food poisoning from an event (option C), Toxic chemical poisoning from an industrial accident (option B)
Sex worker infected with gonorrhea, Outbreak of cholera due to contaminated well water

The epidemic of yellow fever (arthropod vector) is an example of a propagated epidemic (Option D) that result from transmission of the infectious agent over a prolonged duration of time. Cases occur over more than one incubation period.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The recent Air Quality Index (AQI) in Delhi was reported to be 250. Which of the following parameters is included in the calculation of AQI?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Lead

Lead is likely to be elevated as it is the only parameter considered out of the given options while calculating the AQI.

Air Quality Index (AQI) is a tool used for effective communication of air quality status on a scale that is easily comprehensible. Complex air quality data of various pollutants are compiled to give a single score (index value), nomenclature and colour that determines the air pollution of that particular location.

Eight pollutants are taken into consideration to calculate the AQI -

• PM10 (Airborne particulate matter with a diameter of 10 microns or less)
• PM2.5 (Airborne particulate matter with a diameter of 2.5 microns or less)
• NO2 (Nitrogen dioxide)
• SO2 (Sulfur dioxide)
• CO (Carbon monoxide)
• O3 (Ozone/Trioxygen)
• NH3 (Ammonia)
• Pb (Lead)

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Nayi Pahel kits are distributed to newly wedded couples under the family planning programme. Which of the following items is present in the kit?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Urine pregnancy kits

Urine pregnancy kits are present in the Nayi Pahel kits distributed to newly wedded couples for a subsidised fee of Rs 220 under the family planning programme - Mission Parivar Vikas.

It is a family planning kit consisting of -

• Jute bag with the family planning programme logo
• Marriage registration form
• A pamphlet containing information on contraception, family planning, how to use UPT kits and ASHA schemes
• Pack of 3 male condom(Nirodh) x 2 units
• Mala-N oral contraceptive pills x 2 packs
• 3 emergency contraceptive pills called E pills
• 2 pregnancy testing kits
• A grooming or hygiene kit consisting mirror, lipstick, bindi, etc
• An information card with details on respective ASHAs and nearest ANMs

The ASHA is incentivized 100/kit distributed to newly wedded couples.

Antara (Intramuscular injectable contraceptive-DMPA) and Chhaya (oral contraceptive Centchroman) were launched by the Government under its Mission Parivar Vikas but are not part of the Nayi Pahel kits.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is not a principle of health education?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Drawing conclusions

Drawing conclusions is not a principle of health education.

Principles of Health Education:

(Mnemonic: PLS, Good Friend, CLICK MoRe!)

• Participation
• Learning by doing
• Setting an example
• Good human relations
• Feedback
• Credibility
• Leaders
• Interest
• Comprehension

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The non-communicable disease (NCD) clinic at the district hospital screens people above the age of 50 years with positive family history for diabetes. What type of screening is this?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. High-risk screening

The non-communicable disease/ NCD clinic at the district hospital screening people above the age of 50 years for diabetes is a type of high-risk screening.

Screening is searching or testing for diseases or defects that are not evident in apparently healthy individuals. High-risk or selective screening is screening applied selectively to high-risk groups defined on the basis of epidemiological research. For example, screening the other members in families of patients with diabetes or hypertension that tend to aggregate in families. It is an effective and economical method of screening.

Other options:

Option A: Mass screening is the screening of a population or a sub-group of the population for a disease irrespective of the particular risk an individual may run of contracting the disease in question. It is not a useful preventive measure unless there is a  suitable treatment that alters the duration or outcome of a disease.

Option B: Multiphasic screening is the application of two or more screening tests (instead of carrying out separate screening tests for a single disease) to a large number of people in the form of health questionnaires, clinical examinations, and investigations. It has not shown any benefit to the population in terms of mortality and morbidity reduction and has instead increased the cost of health services.

Option C: Prospective screening is screening people for the benefit of others. For example, screening immigrants for infectious diseases such as tuberculosis to protect the home population from the disease.

Note: Prescriptive screening is defined as the presumptive screening of patients for unrecognized diseases for their own benefit. It usually does not arise from a patient's request. Examples include screening for bacteriuria in pregnancy and screening for hemolytic disease in a neonate.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text:
Match the objective of each phase of a clinical trial with the phase.

Column I

1. Indications are finalized and guidelines formulated
2. Drug interactions and long-term adverse effects assessed
3. Efficacy and dose-ranging are determined
4. Assessment of safety and tolerability

Column II

A. Phase I

B. Phase II

C. Phase III

D. Phase IV
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 1- C, 2-D, 3-B, 4-A

The correct answer is 1- C, 2-D, 3-B, and 4-A.

The phases of a clinical trial and their objectives are as given below.

Phase 1 (first in humans) is carried out in 10-100 participants. It aims to test the safety and tolerability of the drug. Usually, healthy volunteers are chosen. Sometimes patients with an advanced or rare disease are also considered. It generally lasts for 1-2 years.

Phase 2 (first in patients) checks the efficacy and dose-ranging of the drug. 50-500 patient subjects receive the experimental drug. It lasts for 2-3 years.

Phase 3 (multisite trial) is carried out for confirmation of the efficacy tested in phase 2. The indications are finalized and guidelines for therapeutic use are formulated. A few hundred to a few thousand patient subjects receive the drug. It lasts for around 3-5 years.

Phase 4 (postmarketing surveillance) tests for adverse effects, or those that occur only after long-term use and drug interactions. It is done in patients already on treatment with the approved drug. There is no fixed duration for this stage.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which amongst the following can be used to treat kesari dal toxicity?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Vitamin C

Vitamin C in doses of 500-1000 mg can be used for the prevention and treatment of lathyrism (kesari dal toxicity).

Lathyrism is a paralyzing disease of humans and animals. It is due to the consumption of khesari dal or Lathyrus sativus. When the husk is removed, it looks similar to red gram or Bengal gram. It is mostly consumed by poor agricultural laborers because it is relatively cheap. Lathyrism is more prevalent in parts of Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Odisha, and Bihar. The Prevention of Food Adulteration Act in India has banned Lathyrus sativus in all forms (whole/ split/ flour).

In humans, it is referred to as neurolathyrism because it affects the nervous system. It is characterized by gradually developing spastic paralysis of the lower limbs. Beta-oxalyl amino alanine (BOAA) is the toxic compound causing this disease. It is water-soluble and can be removed by the following methods:

• Soaking pulses in hot water and discarding the water
• Overnight soaking in lime water, followed by boiling
• Parboiling - for large-scale detoxification

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 35-year-old rice farmer presented with a high-grade fever, diarrhea, seizures, tremors, and vomiting. The physician suspects an illness transmitted by the mosquito shown below. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Japanese encephalitis

The rice farmer presents with features of acute encephalitis and non-specific features like fever, cough, and diarrhea, and is most likely suspected to have Japanese encephalitis. The image shown is of the Culex species of mosquito due to unspotted wings and hunched back, which is a vector of Japanese encephalitis.

Culex mosquitoes:

They are vectors or carriers for Bancroftian filariasis, Japanese encephalitis, West Nile fever, and viral arthritis.

In the larval stage, they are suspended with heads downwards at an angle, a siphon tube is present, and there is an absence of palmate hairs. They lay the eggs in clusters, and adult mosquitoes have their wings unspotted with hunched back.

Various mosquito larvae are shown in the image below. Siphon tube is present in Aedes and Culex, whereas, it is absent in Anopheles.

Other options:

Option A: Anopheles mosquito is the vector for malaria.

Option B: Anopheles mosquito/Mansoni Mosquito could be the vectors for filariasis.

Option C: Aedes mosquito is the vector for yellow fever.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The Sustainable Development Goals(SDG's) are under which health organisation?
options: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. United Nations Development Programme

Sustainable Development Goals(SDG's) are under the United Nations Development Programme.

SDG comprises of 17 goals and 170 targets for Agenda 2030.

The sustainable development goals adopted in 2015 aim to reduce the under 5 mortality to as low as 25 per 1000 live births by the year 2030.

The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), also known as the Global Goals, were adopted by the United Nations in 2015 as a call to action to end poverty, protect the planet, and ensure that by 2030 all people enjoy peace and prosperity.

It consists of 17 integrated sustainable development goals to be achieved by the year 2030 with priority being given to countries that are furthest behind. The SDGs are designed to end poverty, hunger, AIDS, and discrimination against women and girls.

SDG 3 deals with ensuring healthy lives and promoting wellbeing for all at all ages. The important sub-targets of SDG 3 are:

Sub-target
Goal

3.1
Reduce global maternal mortality to <70/100,000 live births.

3.2

• Reduce neonatal mortality to at least as low as 12/1000 live births.
• Reduce under 5 mortality to at least as low as 25/1000 live births.

3.3
End epidemics of AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria, and neglected tropical diseases, combat hepatitis, water-borne diseases, and other communicable diseases

3.5
Prevention and treatment of substance abuse, narcotic abuse, and harmful use of alcohol.

3.7
Universal access to sexual and reproductive health care services, including family planning.

3.9
Substantially reduce deaths and illnesses due to hazardous chemicals and air, water, and soil pollution and contamination.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: While testing the deleterious health hazards on a group of people after giving a new drug and a placebo, the following results were obtained as tabulated. Based on these results, which of the following is true?
options: Absolute risk reduction (ARR) is 10% and relative risk reduction (RRR) is 0.9
Absolute risk reduction (ARR) is 1% and relative risk reduction (RRR) is 10
Absolute risk reduction (ARR) is 10% and relative risk reduction (RRR) is 9
Absolute risk reduction (ARR) is 1% and relative risk reduction (RRR) is 0.1
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Absolute risk reduction (ARR) is 1% and relative risk reduction (RRR) is 0.1

• Lets reconstruct the design table in the following way:

Health hazard (+)
Health hazard (-)
Total

New drug
1603 (a)
13622 (b)
15225 (a+b)

Placebo
1804 (c)
13421 (d)
15225 (c+d)

• Relative risk (RR) is given as a/(a+b) ÷c/(c+d).
• In this scenario, RR = 1603/15225 ÷ 1804/15225 = 0.106/0.118 = 0.89, which is can be rounded up to 0.90. Thus RR = 0.90.
• Relative risk reduction (RRR) = 1 – Relative risk. In this scenario, RRR = 1 – 0.9 = 0.1 or 10%.
• Incidence of a disease is the absolute risk of contracting it.
• Absolute risk rate of group using new drug = 1603/15225 = 0.106 or 10.6% = 11%. The absolute risk rate of group using placebo = 1804/15225 = 0.118 or 11.8% = 12%.
• Absolute risk reduction (ARR) is the difference in the absolute risk rates between the placebo and the drug.
• In this scenario, ARR = 12% - 11% = 1%.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following agency provides seed and manure in applied nutrition programs in schools?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. UNICEF

UNICEF provides seed and manure in applied nutrition programs in schools.

Applied Nutrition Program is implemented with the aim of producing various types of productive food by the community for the community itself.

UNICEF assists the program by providing implements, seeds, manure, and water supply equipment. If free land is available in schools, the facilities provided by UNICEF should be used in developing school gardens.

The produce obtained from the gardens can be utilized for school feeding programs and for nutrition education.

Another strategy called GOBI was also implemented by UNICEF with the aim of a child health revolution.

The GOBI-FFF strategy was given by United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF).

• The GOBI-FFF strategy is aimed at child health revolution and survival.
• It was called initially called the GOBI strategy, and the FFF aspect was later added to it.

Other options:

Option A: CARE- Cooperative for Assistance and Relief Everywhere aims at providing food for children in the age group of 6-11 years. It is also helping in projects like integrated nutrition and health project, better health and nutrition projects, anemia control projects, etc.

Option B: UNDP- The United Nations Development Program provides funds for technical assistance. Its main objective is to help poorer nations in developing their human and natural resources.

Option D: WHO- World Health Organization aims at the attainment of the highest level of health by all people, which helps them to lead a socially and economically productive life.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A young woman working in the printing industry is likely to suffer from infertility due to which of the following toxicity?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Lead

A woman working in the printing industry is likely to suffer from infertility due to lead toxicity.

More industrial workers are exposed to lead than to any other toxic metal. Occupational exposure to lead is seen in several industries including the manufacture of storage batteries, glass,  shipbuilding,  printing, potteries, and rubber industries.

The effects of lead poisoning include abdominal colic, blue-line on the gums, stippling of red cells, anemia, wrist & foot drop,  headache, and convulsions. In young or pregnant women, prolonged lead exposure can cause miscarriages, stillbirth, premature births, etc.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The given logo belongs to which of the following programmes?
options: National Programme for Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Disease, and Stroke
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. National Programme for Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Disease, and Stroke

The image shows the logo of the National Programme for Prevention & Control of Non-Communicable Diseases (NP-NCD), which was earlier called the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Disease, and Stroke (NPCDCS).

NPCDCS was launched in 2010 in order to prevent and control major NCD (non-communicable diseases). It focuses on strengthening infrastructure, human resource development, health promotion, early diagnosis, management, and referral.

Under NPCDCS, NCD Clinics are being set up at District and CHC levels, to provide services for early diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up for common NCD. NPCDCS has specialized facilities at the district hospital level. At the subcentre level under NPCDCS, screening and referral are done.

The NPCDCS has separate components for cancer and other non-communicable diseases like diabetes, and stroke. It has been implemented in over 100 districts in 21 states. For the cancer component, there is the Tertiary Care Cancer Centers (TCCC) scheme, which aims at setting up/strengthening State Cancer Institutes (SCI) and TCCCs all over the country, for providing comprehensive cancer care in the country.

Note: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) has been integrated with this programme in 2021.

Other options:

Option A: The logo below shows Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram

Option C: The logo below shows Ayushman Bharat-National Health Protection Mission

Option D: The logo below shows Family Planning Campaign

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Vaccination against which of the following organisms should be administered post-splenectomy?
options: Haemophilus influenzae B, Staphylococcus aureus, Influenza
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Meningococcus, Haemophilus influenzae B, Pneumococcus

All post-splenectomy patients need to be vaccinated against pneumococcus, meningococcus C (both repeated every 5 years), and H. influenza type B (Hib) (repeated every 10 years).

If an elective splenectomy is planned, prophylactic vaccinations must be given at least 2 weeks before the elective surgery. In case of an emergency splenectomy, patients should be vaccinated as soon as possible after recovery from surgery but before discharge from the hospital.

The following vaccines are given :

• Pneumococcal vaccine: A dose of PCV13 followed by PPSV23 ≥8 weeks later is advised. Revaccinate every five to seven years thereafter.
• H. influenzae type b vaccine: A single dose of Hib vaccine is recommended. Revaccination is not needed for Hib.
• Meningococcal vaccination: Two doses of the MenACWY vaccine are given ≥8 weeks apart. Revaccination is needed every five years.
• Influenza vaccination: Vaccination against seasonal influenza should be given annually.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The provision of 100% biodegradable sanitary napkins for Rs.1 per pad at Janaushadhi Kendras under the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana is known as?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Suvidha

Suvidha is the program aimed at the provision of 100% biodegradable sanitary napkins under Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana.

Low-cost hygienic oxy-biodegradable sanitary napkins were made available for Rs.1 per pad at over 7,900 Janaushadhi Kendras for the underprivileged women of India. The program aims to ensure ‘Swachhta, Swasthya, and Suvidha' for underprivileged women and to improve menstrual hygiene practices throughout the country.

Other options:

Option B: Freedays is the provision of a pack of 6 sanitary napkins for 6 Rupees by the ASHA worker through the Menstrual Hygiene Scheme under the Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram (RKSK).

Option C: Saathiya is a government initiative launched to provide a platform for communication regarding adolescent age-related health issues. Saathiya, meaning a good friend, are peer educators trained by the government with the help of the Saathiya salah mobile application. These Saathiyas act as a catalyst for generating demand for adolescent health services and imparting age-appropriate knowledge on key adolescent health issues to their peer groups.

Option D: Sabla is an empowerment scheme for adolescent girls of age group 11 to 18 years to improve their nutritional and health status under the Integrated child development services scheme (ICDS).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In the following natural history of disease flowchart, point A to C is called?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Lead time

The period between the first possible time of detection (point A) and the usual time of diagnosis (point C) is called as lead time.

Other options:

The period between the first possible time of detection (point A) and the final critical point of diagnosis (point B) is called Screening time.

Screening is the search for unrecognized diseases or defects in apparently healthy individuals by means of rapidly applicable tests or procedures. It must be done in conditions where there is a considerable time lag between the onset of the disease and the usual time of diagnosis (point C in the image).

This ensures the success of any treatment in reversing the disease process. The final critical point (point B in the image) is the stage beyond which treatment would be unsuccessful or there would be permanent damage.

Generation time is defined as the interval of time between the onset of infection by a host and the maximal infectivity of that host.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A family brings in their child who is suffering from diarrhoea to the PHC. Oral Rehydration Solution is not available currently. Which among the following options will you advise them till the ORS mixture is obtained?
options: Dilute the child's usual diet and feed him.
Give the child a mixture of 1 teaspoon of table salt and 2 teaspoons of sugar in 1 L of drinking water.
Give the child salted rice water or soup
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Give the child salted rice water or soup

Salted rice water or salted yoghurt drinks must be given when ORS is not available.

Many countries have designated recommended house fluids. Wherever possible these should include at least one fluid that contains salt. Fluids that do not contain salt are water in which a cereal has been cooked e.g. rice water; unsalted soup, yoghurt drinks, green coconut water, weak tea etc. The mothers should be taught to add salt about 3 g/litre to an unsalted drink or soup during diarrhoea

What do we advise the family to do when ORS is not available?

To- do:

• If the WHO mixture is not available, a simple mixture of 1 teaspoon of table salt and 6 teaspoons of sugar must be dissolved in 1 L of drinking water and given to the child.
• Add 3g/litre of salt to an unsalted drink or soup.
• The infant's usual diet of cereals, vegetables and other foods should be continued and never be diluted. The child should be given as much nutrient-rich food as acceptable.

Avoid:

• Sweetened drinks with sugar, like commercial fruit juices and sweetened tea, as they lead to osmotic diarrhoea and hypernatremia.
• Fluids with a stimulant and purgative effect like coffee and medicinal tea infusions.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: As an intern in the community medicine department, you are asked to study the various graphical representations of data. What is the following graph best used for?
options: Correlating risk factors of a disease
Studying the periodic trends of disease over time
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Survival time analysis

The graph depicted is a Kaplan-Meir plot and the use of the graph is survival time analysis.

Survival time analysis includes studying of -

• What is the survival time of patients with a given disease.
• How does this survival time compare between two groups of patients given different treatments for the same disease.
• Among those who survive up to a certain time, at what time or rate can they be expected to die.
• What factors, such as risk factors or treatments, affect the survival time.

Despite its name, survival analysis can be used to help answer questions of this kind about any kind of event, not just death—such as how long it takes before a hip replacement fails, how long it takes before a patient has a second heart attack, or how long it takes for coronary stents to become re-stenosed.

Other options -

Option A: The line of best fit is used to express a relationship in a scatter plot of different data points as a straight line rather than multiple dots. It is an output of regression analysis and can be used as a prediction tool.

Option C: Scatter diagrams are used to correlate risk factors of the disease and present as positive correlation, negative correlation or no correlation.

Option D: A line diagram is used to study the periodic trends of a disease over time.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The aim of Kyoto protocol is ______
options: To promote proper bio-medical waste disposal
To promote clean water and sanitation.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. To mitigate greenhouse gas emissions.

The aim of the Kyoto protocol is to mitigate greenhouse gas emissions.

The Kyoto Protocol is associated with the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) regime. It covers the emission of the following six greenhouse gases:

• Nitrous oxide (N2O)
• Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs)
• Perfluorocarbons (PFCs)
• Sulphur hexafluoride (SF6)

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The quality of drinking water is considered to be satisfactory if the presumptive coliform count is:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Less than 10/100 mL

According to WHO guidelines, the quality of drinking water is considered to be satisfactory if the presumptive coliform count is 0/100 mL.

Drinking water should not contain any pathogenic organisms or bacteria indicative of faecal contamination. The primary bacterial indicator used to assess this is the coliform group of organisms. This is because they are present abundantly in the human intestine and can be easily detected by culture methods.

The presumptive coliform test can be done by the multiple tube method or membrane filtration techniques. In the multiple-tube method, the water to be tested is inoculated into tubes containing a suitable liquid medium. These tubes are then incubated for 48 hours and examined. The test is called presumptive because the reaction observed in the tube may occasionally be due to other organisms. The presumption that the reaction is due to coliform organisms has to be confirmed. McConkey's lactose bile salt broth with bromocresol purple 25 as an indicator is used as the media. Escherichia coli or thermotolerant coliform bacteria should not be detected in any 100 ml sample.

In samples of chlorinated water, confirmation of the presumptive test is necessary. This is done by subculturing the positive tubes in two tubes of brilliant green bile broth. It is based on the fact that E.Coli is the only coliform that can produce gas from lactose at 44°C.

Supplementary indicator organisms include fecal streptococci and sulfite-reducing clostridia.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A patient is brought to the emergency room after being evacuated from a collapsed building during an earthquake. He is unconscious and has a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 8. Imaging of the head reveals the following findings. Which color code will you triage him in?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Red

The CT scan finding of a biconvex lentiform hyperdensity that does not cross suture lines is suggestive of an extradural hematoma. With a GCS score of 8, the patient should be triaged as red as management requires emergency surgery.

Triage is done based on a preliminary assessment of patients to determine the urgency of treatment. Patients are prioritized based on the severity of their injuries and the likelihood of survival with prompt medical treatment. It is particularly useful in case of mass casualties to prevent health facilities from getting overwhelmed.

Red indicated a high priority of treatment or an immediate transfer to higher health facilities. These patients may survive if they receive timely medical intervention.

An extradural hematoma with a GCS score of < or = 8 necessitates emergent surgery in the form of craniotomy, hematoma evacuation, and ligation of the injured vessel. Early surgery is associated with good neurological outcomes.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: During a rural outreach program, you interact with a 28-year-old female and her 2-year-old son. You notice that the mother appears lean and on examination find that she has pallor. Her son’s current weight for age is below the 50th percentile. Which national program would you educate these patients about?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. POSHAN Abhiyaan

As the key issues identified in the mother and her son are anemia and malnutrition, they are part of the target population of the POSHAN Abhiyaan program.

The goals of the POSHAN Abhiyaan programme are:

• Prevent and reduce undernutrition and stunting in children aged 0-6 years.
• Reduce the prevalence of anemia among children aged 6 months - 6 years.
• Reduce the prevalence of anemia among women and adolescent girls aged 15-49 years.
• Reduce low birth weight.

Other Options:

Option A: The Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK) has provisions for free transport of pregnant women and sick infants from:

• home to the health facilities
• between facilities in case of a referral
• back home from the health facilities

Option B: Kishori Shakti Yojana (KSY) seeks to empower adolescent girls, so as to enable them to take charge of their lives. The objectives are to:

• improve the nutritional, health and development status of adolescent girls
• promote awareness of health, hygiene, nutrition and family care
• opportunities for learning life skills
• going back to school
• help them gain a better understanding of their social environment
• take initiatives to become productive members of society.

Option D: Nikshay Poshan Yojana is a government scheme in India to provide Rs.500 per month for TB patients to buy food.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text:
Which of the following are components of the physical quality of life index (PQLI)?

1. Infant mortality rate
2. Life expectancy at birth
3. Literacy rate
4. Life expectancy at 1 year of age
5. Under 5 mortality rate
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 1,3 and 4

Infant mortality rate, literacy rate, and life expectancy at 1 year of age are the components of the physical quality of life index (PQLI).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: An auxiliary nurse midwife conducting a vaccination camp received 2 vaccine vials. One is a pentavalent vaccine and the other is an MR vaccine, which she opened on the day of the camp. She intends to reuse these vials by storing them in proper condition, at her next vaccination camp to be conducted in 2 weeks. What would you advise her regarding the re-utilization of these vials?
options: Use MR vaccine and discard pentavalent vaccine
Use pentavalent vaccine and discard MR vaccine
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Use pentavalent vaccine and discard MR vaccine

She can use the pentavalent vaccine and discard the MR vaccine.  According to the open vial policy, the pentavalent vaccine can be reused, whereas MR can not be reused.

Open vial policy allows for the reuse of partially used multidose vials of applicable vaccines under the Universal Immunization Programme in subsequent sessions for up to 4 weeks subject to certain conditions and thereby reducing vaccine wastage.

It is applicable only for DPT, TT, hepatitis B vaccine, OPV and liquid pentavalent vaccine.

It is not applicable for BCG, measles, rotavirus vaccines and JE vaccines.

Vaccine vials opened in session-site can be use in more than one session up to four weeks if expiry date has not passed, if storage and transport was appropriate, no contamination has occurred in vial septum, asepsis in withdrawing was practiced and if vaccine vial monitor has not reached discard point.

Open vials should not be submerged in water.

Ensure all opened vials have recorded date and time of opening.

At the end of a session, all vaccines should be returned to the cold chain point and segregated as re-usable and non-reusable.

All open vials of BCG, measles and JE must be destroyed after 48 hours or before next session, whichever is earlier.

In case of any adverse events following immunization, all open vials should not be discarded until investigation is complete.

All vials must be transported in zipper bags in the vaccine carrier and recorded in stock register.

Ice packs used should be well sealed.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What is the primary goal of the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme?
options: To promote healthy lifestyle choices among individuals
To collect monthly disease surveillance data
To detect early warning signals of outbreaks
To conduct research on rare diseases
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. To detect early warning signals of outbreaks

The main purpose of Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme (IDSP) is to detect early warning signals of outbreaks.

IDSP (formely known as Integrated Disease Surveillance Project)  is a national decentralised state-based surveillance program. The mission is to detect early warning signals for timely and effective public health action so that it can be initiated against outbreaks of prone diseases in both urban and rural areas. It also provides essential data to monitor ongoing disease control programs.

The program includes a Central Surveillance Unit, State Surveillance Units, and District Surveillance Units, and collects weekly disease surveillance data (Option B) on epidemic-prone diseases from reporting units such as hospitals and medical colleges. The data is analyzed for disease trends and investigated by a Rapid Response Team consisting of specialists whenever there is a rising trend of illness.

The surveillance is necessary to recognize cases or clusters of cases, access the public health impact of health events, demonstrate the need for public health intervention programs, monitor the effectiveness of prevention and control measures, and identify high-risk groups or geographical areas for targeted interventions.
